content.title: ORGAN FOOD CHEAT SHEET NOBODY TEACHES YOU IN SCHOOL
facts: **BEETS** are good for LIVER – they contain betaine, which helps your liver flush out toxins instead of letting them build up.
**SARDINES** are good for BRAIN – a 3 oz serving 2x/week delivers omega-3s that keep the fatty sheath around your neurons intact.
**ASPARAGUS** are good for KIDNEYS – it acts as a natural diuretic, helping flush excess salt and fluid instead of letting it pool.
**PUMPKIN SEEDS** are good for PROSTATE – 1 oz/day is packed with zinc, a mineral linked to healthy prostate tissue.
**OATS** are good for HEART – 1 cup/day of beta-glucan fiber grabs cholesterol in your gut and drags it out before it hits your arteries.
**BONE BROTH** is good for GUT LINING – the collagen and gelatin help seal and soothe the intestinal wall instead of leaving it irritated.
**LIVER (BEEF OR CHICKEN)** is good for THYROID – it's one of the richest food sources of selenium, a mineral your thyroid needs to make hormones properly.
**BLUEBERRIES** are good for EYES – ½ cup/day of anthocyanins support the tiny blood vessels behind your retina.
**FENNEL** is good for DIGESTION – chewing a few seeds after a meal relaxes gut muscles and eases trapped gas.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
A few of these deserve more explanation than a single line can give. Beets get their liver-support reputation from betaine, a compound that helps your liver process fat and keeps bile flowing smoothly instead of getting sluggish. Sardines are one of the few foods where you get omega-3s attached to calcium-rich bones, so you're feeding your brain and your skeleton in the same bite. And pumpkin seeds don't just supply zinc — they also carry plant compounds called phytosterols that researchers have linked to healthier prostate tissue over time. Everyone's body responds a little differently, so pay attention to what actually works for you.

This is what we do over at @smarthealthfix — breaking down nutrition, common health issues, organ function, and small daily habits into things you can actually use. Our mission is to help you build small, realistic changes instead of chasing quick fixes that never stick.
